This is a microscope view showing stem tissue with many tiny dark dots/specks on tan/bleached fibrous tissue. This pattern strongly suggests fungal microsclerotia or pycnidia on stem tissue. Top candidates: **Charcoal_Rot** (microsclerotia), **Phomopsis/Diaporthe** (pycnidia on stem).

Let me check reference images for these candidates.

The test image shows a microscope view of soybean stem tissue with densely scattered tiny black dots on tan/bleached fibrous tissue. This is the classic appearance of **microsclerotia** of *Macrophomina phaseolina*.

Key evidence:
- Circular microscope field of view
- Bleached/tan stem tissue with fibrous longitudinal structure
- Numerous tiny, uniform black dots (microsclerotia) densely distributed throughout
- This is the pathognomonic feature of Charcoal Rot — the "charcoal" appearance comes from these microsclerotia

The Charcoal_Rot reference confirms bleached stems with dark internal tissue. No other class (Phomopsis shows larger circular pycnidia on pods; Fusarium shows vascular browning; Brown_Stem_Rot shows internal brown discoloration without tiny dots) matches this microscopic pattern.
